convoLines.text: "The pantry's nearly bare. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Meet me at the ridge above the creek and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"We went over this," Tyrone says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
Their voice loosens. The guardedness thins.
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
"Still on that favor."
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
"The pantry's nearly bare. Come forage with me tomorrow — two of us can fill packs."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the meadow edge, west of the creek in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"The whole fire was arguing about Cliffhanger last night — what to even CALL it. 'Ugly-Eyes' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Names are for when it's dead or known. Right now it's neither, so I count portions out loud before eating instead."
"We'll land on something. We always do — usually the loudest person's idea."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright, love. Go do what you need to do."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about that favor — we got cut off, 5 days back. 'We're done for now. Not done-done. For now.'"
"It's already handled. Thank you for asking."
"Still on that favor. That's still where we are."
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"That again?" Tyrone sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
"This was good." They mean it.
Paper's scarce, so I write small. History doesn't need big letters.
Ines has an edge today — something curdled.
"I record the arguments too. Especially the arguments. That's the real history."
"My notes are a mess. Future scholars will hate me. They'll still read them."
"Still on what they want."
"Right. Sorry, I go on about it. What did you want?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Duc always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Listen to me — We never finished talking about that favor — we got cut off, 6 days back. '...Okay. I'll figure it out. They won't ask twice. That much is clear.'"
"Huh. I wouldn't have guessed that about you."
"Still on that question."
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Tyrone digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1936 kcal to the pantry.)
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "They took Ines and Ursula — The Auction, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Anyway." A small smile.
You show them Pawpaw — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Go. But sit with what I said."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"About the pantry run — still need hands. Are you in?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "They took me. The Auction — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
It's quiet at the tree line. Ines doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Like I said — Still on what's been happening."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
"Can I tell you something? I don't actually know how to swim and I'm terrified someone will find out."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on their secret."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The whole fire was arguing about Nightlight last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Loud Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Give it three more days of arguing. Then someone says the obvious thing and we all pretend it was theirs."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"That's enough for now. It'll percolate."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Can I tell you something? At night I talk to someone who isn't there anymore."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
You walk to the cache spot with Mabel. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"Okay." Mabel looks down. "Okay, you got me. I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. I wasn't protecting myself. I was protecting someone else." Their voice is small.
Mabel looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Mabel rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on their secret. That's the priority."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I trust you? I mean really."
"Okay." Something shutters, just slightly.
"Still on whether they can trust you."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Brian — The Blood Tithe, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Pantry's thin and getting thinner. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the far treeline, past the rocks."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. I know the far treeline, past the rocks — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Watch for this: It doesn't move. Speedbump, every time. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."
"This one — Senegal Date Palm. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"The Blood Tithe. They just... took Brian. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
You show them Moringa — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I sharpen sticks down to nothing. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"The plan is the plan until it isn't. Then we make a new one."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.

recoverHome: d10: That night, they bring Duc home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d9: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d9: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."
